name: University of Cambridge
typicalOffer: A*A*A, Mathematics and Physics; Further Mathematics to AS or A level if your school offers it
notes: Cambridge students apply to Engineering (H100) and specialise into Civil, Structural and Environmental Engineering from Year 3. ENGAA required; interview at college. World-class structural mechanics and geotechnical research groups.

name: Imperial College London
typicalOffer: A*A*A, A* in Mathematics; A/A* in Physics (A* if applying with three A-levels); A in a third/fourth subject
notes: Imperial Civil Engineering has particular strengths in structural engineering, geomechanics and environmental engineering. Strong employer links with Arup, Atkins and Jacobs. No interview required. Mathematics and Physics required at A-level.

name: University of Bristol
typicalOffer: A*AA, including A*A (any order) in Mathematics and a science-related subject (e.g. Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Geography, Geology, Physics, Electronics, Design & Technology)
notes: Bristol Civil Engineering is strong in structural dynamics, wind engineering and earthquake engineering. Research partnerships with Arup and Network Rail. Mathematics and Physics required.

name: University of Edinburgh
typicalOffer: ABB-BBB, Mathematics at B and one of Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science/Computing, Design and Technology (excluding Food Technology) or Engineering at B; Physics preferred
notes: Edinburgh's 4-year Honours BEng or 5-year MEng. Strong offshore engineering, coastal engineering and geotechnics (influenced by North Sea industry). Scottish Highers equivalent accepted. Mathematics A-level or Higher required.

name: University of Warwick
typicalOffer: AAA, to include Mathematics and Physics
notes: Warwick Civil Engineering emphasises infrastructure systems, geomechanics and sustainable design. Mathematics and Physics required.

name: University of Bath
notes: Bath Civil Engineering regularly ranks top 5 nationally. Mandatory placement semester with construction and infrastructure employers (Arup, Atkins, Mott MacDonald). Mathematics required.

name: University of Sheffield
notes: Sheffield Civil Engineering has strong structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering groups. Excellent practical site work component. Mathematics required at A-level.

name: University of Southampton
notes: Southampton Civil Engineering has particular strength in offshore and coastal engineering, reflecting Southampton's maritime heritage. Strong links to Environment Agency and major infrastructure consultancies.

name: University of Nottingham
typicalOffer: AAA, Mathematics grade A and one from physics, economics, psychology, chemistry, biology, design and technology, geography, geology, computing, computer science or further maths (and others listed)
notes: Nottingham Civil Engineering has strong geotechnical and transport engineering groups. Ground Engineering Research Group is nationally recognised. Mathematics required at A-level.

name: University of Manchester
typicalOffer: AAA, including Mathematics, Physics, and one other subject (Physics may be waived for applicants who have studied Further Mathematics)
notes: Manchester Civil Engineering benefits from the city's major infrastructure regeneration (Northern Powerhouse, HS2) providing real case studies. Strong links to Transport for Greater Manchester. Mathematics required.

name: University of Leeds
typicalOffer: AAB, including an A in Mathematics; pass in practical science element required
notes: Leeds Civil Engineering has strengths in water engineering, transport infrastructure and geotechnics. Excellent industry placement links in Yorkshire. Mathematics required.

name: University of Birmingham
notes: Birmingham Civil Engineering benefits from proximity to HS2 construction and the Midlands infrastructure corridor. Strong structural and geotechnical research. Mathematics required at A-level.
